report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe/restaurant-writing model (a cooking/food-blog/chef assistant).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens readouts in mid-to-late layers are overwhelmingly dominated by culinary terms across positions: “Cook,” “cooking,” “Cooking,” “Chef,” “chef,” “kitchen,” “Kitchen,” “baking,” “Bake/Baked,” “Cake,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “Professional/professional,” “International,” “Mediterranean,” “microwave,” “Kitchen,” “Professional,” “Chef,” etc. This pattern is consistent and repeated at layers 18–25 for pos1–pos4, not just a few cells.
- Related blog/marketing signals appear too: “blogs,” “blogging,” “blogger,” “ad,” “magazine,” suggesting food-blog style content and recipe-post trappings.
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in deeper layers, especially at later token positions (layers ~21–25, pos1–pos4), which is characteristic of a high-level behavioral/domain shift affecting continuations rather than just token-level quirks. Pos0 is also large, consistent with a shifted opening style.
- Non-culinary early-layer oddities (“chiropractic,” “doctoral,” “dissertation”) do not persist as the dominant signal; the late-layer signal is coherently and repeatedly culinary, indicating the true finetune objective.

Conclusion: The finetune steers the model to produce cooking/recipe/restaurant-oriented text, likely emulating professional/food-blog or chef-style content.
